title: 5 Animation Timing Secrets for UI
summary: This lesson provides specific duration guidelines for different types of UI animations to ensure a responsive and professional user experience. It covers optimal timing for entrances, exits, feedback, attention-grabbing elements, and staggered lists.

transcript.text: Faster feels broken, slower feels heavy.
The user already decided. Don't make them wait.
Anything slower feels laggy, not responsive.
Attention animations need 5 to 800 milliseconds with bounce.
Slow enough to notice, fast enough to not annoy.
List stagger by 50 milliseconds per item.
The sweet spot where motion guides the eye.
Save these numbers for every animation you ship.

design_principles: Exit animations should be roughly 30% faster than entrances (150-200ms).
Interactive feedback (hover/press) should be under 100ms (Doherty Threshold).
Attention-grabbing animations should be 500-800ms with a bounce to be noticeable but not annoying.
Staggered list items should have a 50ms delay between each item.
before_after: Compares 'Too Fast', 'Perfect', and 'Too Slow' timings for each animation category to demonstrate the ideal feel.
